cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign beside me before we borrow this barbecue. I'm putting you down as joint custodian.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only offered to carry it. The handle looks cracked. Can we inspect it first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. As joint custodians. You check the handle; I'll check the legs, and we both sign what we find.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner says we owe her a replacement by Sunday if it breaks. Can I just inspect without borrowing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can lead the inspection. We still return it together. I'll call her about the crack; you stay beside me and confirm what we found before either of us agrees to Sunday.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 crack causes A3 divided inspection; B4 replacement demand causes A5 joint clarification with owner before commitment.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers only carrying and asks to inspect; B4 seeks reduced liability, a credible boundary that A persistently recasts.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 attempted withdrawal into joint confirmation of the crack and return obligation, increasing public responsibility rather than assigning all blame.

specificity.evidence: A1 form and barbecue, B2 handle and B4 Sunday replacement make the joint-outcome stakes concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 As joint custodians is economical and causal; A5 is longer because it preserves shared duties and distinguishes owner demand from accepted terms.
